title: Repair times of two crews
intro:
A utility logged the time (hours) two maintenance crews took to repair the same kind of pump fault: 9 repairs by crew A and 10 by crew B. Repair times are skewed to the right (most are short, a few are very long), and the samples are small, so compare the crews with the **Mann–Whitney U test**. H₀: the two distributions are the same; H₁: they differ (two-sided), at α = 0.05.

Find U₁, the U for crew A (sample 1), and the two-sided p-value from the normal approximation with the continuity correction. U₁ is a whole number; give p to three decimals or more.

Statistic.says: That is U₂, the U for crew B. U₁ and U₂ add to n₁n₂ = 90; the exercise asks U₁, for crew A (sample 1).
That is R₁, the rank sum of crew A. Subtract n₁(n₁ + 1)/2 = 45 to get U₁.

PValue.says: That is the exact p-value, which Python's mannwhitneyu and R's wilcox.test give by default for small samples. The exercise asks the normal approximation: method='asymptotic' in Python, exact = FALSE in R.
You left out the continuity correction. Subtract 0.5 from |U₁ − 45| before dividing by √150.
That is a one-tailed p-value. H₁ is two-sided, so double the tail.
That is the p-value of Welch's t-test on these times. The exercise asks the Mann–Whitney test, which ranks the data.

hints: Rank all 19 times together, from 1 (the shortest, 0.8 h) to 19 (the longest, 9.5 h). There are no ties.
Add the ranks of crew A's nine times: that is R₁. Then U₁ = R₁ − n₁(n₁ + 1)/2 = R₁ − 45.

Under H₀, U has mean n₁n₂/2 = 45 and standard deviation √(n₁n₂(n₁ + n₂ + 1)/12) = √150. With the continuity correction, z = (|U₁ − 45| − 0.5)/√150 and p = 2 × P(Z > z). Python stats.mannwhitneyu(a, b, method='asymptotic'); R wilcox.test(a, b, exact = FALSE).
